newsitem.title: USA: Jury in Oklahoma bomb case recesses for the day.
newsitem.headline: Jury in Oklahoma bomb case recesses for the day.

text.p: The jury in the trial of accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh ended its deliberations on Sunday without reaching a verdict in the case.
The panel of seven men and five women, which started their deliberations on Friday morning, ended on Sunday at midday so they could take a break, said Federal Judge Richard Matsch.

"I'm going to grant your request that you recess deliberations and take the rest of the day off," the judge said when he called the jury into the Denver federal courtroom at noon. "Rest and relax as much as you can."
He told the jury, which is sequestered, to resume its deliberations at 8:30 a.m. MDT (10:30 EDT) (1430 GMT) on Monday.

The jury has spent 2 1/2 days weighing murder and conspiracy charges against McVeigh, 29, a former soldier, who is accused of blowing up the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995. The explosion killed 168 people and wounded more than 500 others.
McVeigh faces the possibility of a death sentence or life in prison if convicted.
